name: Lime plaster (lime putty and marble dust)
summary: Non-hydraulic (air) lime putty laid in coats over masonry and finished with a lime-and-marble-dust setting coat that is trowelled close. It hardens by taking carbon dioxide from the air: the calcium hydroxide of the putty becomes calcite, so the finished skin is a fine calcite body bound by calcite. It is the Rotunda's coffered dome.

formation.how: Limestone is burnt to quicklime, slaked with water and sieved to lime putty, which is matured before use. Putty is mixed with sharp sand for the backing coats (coarse stuff) and with fine sand or marble dust for the finish (setting stuff). After laying, the putty carbonates: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 -> CaCO3 + H2O. Carbonation turns portlandite into calcite and changes the pore structure.

specularF0.derivation: normal-incidence Fresnel reflectance R0 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 over calcite's epsilon (1.486) and omega (1.658) indices; a carbonated finish is a random aggregate of calcite grains, so its F0 lies in this band
specularF0.source: Born, M. & Wolf, E. (1999) Principles of Optics, 7th ed., Cambridge University Press, section 1.5 (reflection and refraction of a plane wave); indices from Handbook of Mineralogy: Calcite, http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/calcite.pdf

boundUpperMarblePowder.note: loose ground white marble (98 % CaCO3, d50 2.6 um): the marble dust of the finish at its whitest; a set plaster scatters less than a loose fine powder and carries binder impurities, so it lies below this bound
boundUpperMarblePowder.source: Omya Pars, Product Information OMYACARB 2-MH (natural calcium carbonate from very high purity white marble, Meymeh plant), edition 27/02/07, https://mychem.ir/uploads/tds/28825.pdf

optics.wet: Water (a far better index match to calcite than air) fills the open pores, so scattering at grain boundaries falls and the surface darkens until it dries; the porosity below sets how much water it takes up.

bayRule.text: The setting coat is laid in two or three thin coats in quick succession, floated as it begins to set and polished with a steel trowel as it hardens, so each field is finished in one working session; the coffers, ribs and bands of the dome bound the fields.
bayRule.source: Napier & Jenkins (2018) Inform Guide: Plain Lime Plastering, Historic Environment Scotland, https://www.historicenvironment.scot/archives-and-research/publications/publication/?publicationId=67d4d72c-7b8c-4622-a244-a94b01090177

photograph: A dense, closed skin with a soft sheen where the steel trowel polished it, and broad, very low clouding where suction and drying were uneven.
Crazing (a fine web of hairline cracks) on a finish that dried too fast; single hairline cracks that follow the structure below.
Arrises of coffers and ribs slightly softened, never machine-sharp; running marks along run members.
Darker grey soiling on upward-facing ledges and in the backs of coffers; patches that read by a slightly different whiteness and texture.

unverified.reason: Attributed to Lawrence, R.M., Mays, T.J., Rigby, S.P., Walker, P. & D'Ayala, D. (2007) Effects of carbonation on the pore structure of non-hydraulic lime mortars. Cement and Concrete Research 37(7), 1059-1069, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconres.2007.04.011 (pore volume said to grow near this diameter as portlandite becomes calcite, by mercury intrusion porosimetry). The citation checker confirmed the paper's title, authors, volume and pages (Crossref), but its abstract and full text are closed and could not be read, so the 0.1 um figure, and whether it is a diameter or a radius, is not confirmed.

unverified.field: luminous reflectance of a clean, dry, carbonated lime-and-marble-dust finish
unverified.reason: No measured value for set lime plaster was found. The range lies below the measured marble-powder bound (0.95) because a set body scatters less than a loose fine powder. The tier (b) ColorChecker specimen sheet must settle it.

unverified.field: specular lobe roughness of a steel-trowelled finish
unverified.reason: No measured BRDF of trowelled lime found; Vitruvius describes well-made polished stucco as taking a mirror-like polish (VII.3.9), so a trowelled finish carries a real specular lobe. Needs a goniometric or tier (b) measurement.
The square-root-of-time law is standard for lime carbonation, but no rate for lime plaster was verified in this search.

unverified.field: area finished in one working session (bay)
unverified.reason: No sourced figure; the dome's coffers and ribs bound the fields.
No measured friction coefficient for a trowelled lime finish was found; the surface is not walked on.
